meta.title: OpenClaw instead of queuing to see a programmer - safe changes to a production site
meta.description: OpenClaw accepts tasks via chat, Codex changes the code, CI/CD checks and deploys the preview, and production is updated only after confirmation.

hero.title: Typical site changes - without a constant queue to the programmer.
hero.lead: An employee sets a task in Telegram or Slack. OpenClaw clarifies the requirements, Codex changes the code in a separate branch, the pipeline runs checks and previews. Only the confirmed version gets into production.
hero.note: The agent does not have free access to the server, secrets and database. Its work is limited by the repository, allowed files, time, budget and mandatory checks.

terminal.request: Add a new tariff, update the FAQ and prepare a publication for today.
steps: Preview is ready. Production is waiting for approval

audience.title: The site is already making money and cannot wait for every small edit
items: hundreds or thousands of visitors per day
regular promotions, tariffs, pages and forms
there is a Git repository and repeatable deploy
the error is noticeable to customers and affects revenue

scenarios.title: What businesses can release via chat

items.title: Texts, tariffs and FAQ
items.text: The manager describes the change with a regular message, receives a preview and publishes it without correspondence with the developer.

items.title: Promo pages and promotions
items.text: OpenClaw assembles the page from the approved components, connects the form and prepares the release for the required date.

items.title: Forms and Notices
items.text: New fields, recipients and texts are added via a verifiable pull request with a submit test.

items.title: SEO and markup
items.text: Title, description, schema.org, redirects and robots are changed only in permitted places and are automatically checked.

items.title: Analytical events
items.text: The event is added to the code and checked in preview before it gets into production analytics.

items.title: Minor fixes
items.text: Codex localizes the problem, writes a regression test and suggests a fix. An unsure case automatically goes to the engineer.

pipeline.title: From message to production without jumping through checks

steps.title: Request
steps.text: Telegram, Slack or internal portal verifies the identity and role of the author.

steps.title: Plan
steps.text: OpenClaw clarifies the problem, identifies the risk, and shows what it intends to change.

steps.title: Isolated work
steps.text: Codex gets a temporary sandbox and a separate branch without production secrets.

steps.title: Checks
steps.text: CI runs formatting, code analysis, tests, assembly and security gates.

steps.title: Preview and approval
steps.text: The customer sees a live page, diff and a clear description of the change.

steps.title: Release
steps.text: A secure workflow performs a deploy, smoke test, and rollback if there is a problem.

providers.name: GitHub Actions
providers.text: Protected branches, environments, required checks, OIDC and deployment approvals.

providers.name: GitLab CI/CD
providers.text: Merge request pipelines, protected environments, review apps and approval rules.

providers.name: Bitbucket Pipelines
providers.text: Deployment environments, branch permissions and manual steps.

providers.name: CircleCI / Jenkins
providers.text: The existing pipeline is preserved; OpenClaw creates a task and reads only the result of the checks.

gates.title: The agent proposes a change. Pipeline decides whether it can be released.

security.title: OpenClaw does not become your company administrator

items.title: Limited repository
items.text: A separate GitHub App or service account sees only the required repo and cannot change branch protection.

items.title: Permitted zones
items.text: For autonomous tasks, an allowlist of directories is specified. Auth, payments, secrets, CI and destructive migrations require an engineer.

items.title: Temporary sandbox
items.text: Each task runs in a clean container or worktree. Once completed, the environment is destroyed.

items.title: No production secrets
items.text: Keys are issued only to CI jobs through secret manager or OIDC and never end up in prompt, diff or chat.

items.title: Tool control
items.text: The commands, network, execution time, number of iterations, and cost of the model are limited by the task policy.

items.title: Confirmation with TTL
items.text: Approval is tied to a specific commit SHA, is one-time only, and expires. It is not possible to change the code after confirmation.

items.title: Full magazine
items.text: The request author, plan, tool calls, diff, CI results, approver, commit and deployment result are saved.

items.title: Kill switch
items.text: With one command, new tasks, merge and deploy are disabled without stopping the site itself.

risk_levels.examples: content, SEO, ready-made blocks, feature flags

risk_levels.approval: engineer does review; standalone deploy is prohibited

production.title: The release should not turn visitors into testers

items.title: No downtime
items.text: Blue-green, canary or rolling deployment is selected for the current infrastructure.

items.title: No dangerous migrations
items.text: Schema changes are released via expand/contract; destructive steps are not performed by the agent.

items.title: Post-deploy check
items.text: Health endpoint, main pages, form, queue and key user path are checked.

items.title: Returning a working version
items.text: If errors increase, smoke test fails, or latency degrades, rollback is enabled.

items.title: Observability
items.text: Errors, logs, traces and release markers are associated with a commit and a specific OpenClaw task.

items.title: Limited rollout
items.text: A risky change is first seen by a small percentage of traffic or only by the internal team.

boundary.title: What does the system replace, and where does the engineer remain?
boundary.agent_title: Can be given to the system
agent_items: release after all checks and approval
human_items: new architecture and complex business logic
a solution that is not covered by tests and policies
boundary.note: The goal is to remove the full-time programmer from the flow of small, predictable tasks, not to pretend that engineering responsibility has disappeared.

offer.title: OpenClaw Release Operator
offer.description: I design and deploy a managed change path on top of your repository and current CI/CD.
features: analysis of the repository, deploy and task types
sandbox, branch policy and approval matrix
monitoring, updates and analysis of failed tasks
offer.note: The exact cost depends on test coverage, number of environments, stack, access requirements and site criticality.

form.description: It is enough to describe the stack, repository, frequency of edits and current deployment. There is no need to submit secrets and access to the form.
